title: Prove an eight-source singleton floor of 28 calls (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Prove **28 <= f(8) <= 32** in the restored binary singleton-connector model, and a **538-query lower bound** for the complete batch of 255 nonzero masks even with arbitrary extra output readouts. The inherited Gray-block construction costs 542 queries. Claim type: scoped written mathematical proof with finite exact corroboration. No new kappa.

```text
Each of 8 coordinate deletions: L-c_i >= f(7) = 24
Sum all 8 inequalities:        7L >= 192
New eight-source floor:        L >= 28
Necessary 28-call counts:      (4,4,4,4,4,4,2,2), up to relabelling
```

Only `research/eight-source-singleton-floor/` is added. Produced by Nick Petalas. conorholds #3058 supplies the seven-source theorem, coordinate-deletion argument and explicit eight-source question. Ross Richardson #943 supplies the dirty connector and paired-prefix criterion; Douglas Colkitt #1185 supplies the Gray-block upper construction. Those predecessors and their classifications/censuses are cited, not audited or replayed as this deliverable. The new step is the summed projection bound and its all-readout batch consequence.

The [advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19146100) proposed a 26-call application of a published covering-code bound. Summing the inherited deletion inequalities gives 28 directly, so the delivered proof needs no new coding-theory premise. Work stopped at that first projection consequence.

## Evidence

Before, #1185's parity pair-count bound permits 24 eight-source calls. After, the written projection proof excludes every source length below 28 and restricts all possible length-28 multiplicities. The full-batch argument also prices absent masks that require at least four readouts.

Local CPython 3.12.15 on Darwin arm64 passes:

- All 10,934 closed words through eight calls on one through four labelled sources and all 147,096 nonempty subset projections.
- All 12,870 positive even eight-source count vectors through total 32; all 1,287 shorter than 28 fail a necessary deletion constraint, and exactly 28 labelled vectors at length 28 meet them.
- The inherited 32-call source word, all 255 paired readouts, all eight seven-source projections and a complete 542-query linear execution on all 528 dirty input basis columns.
- Eleven invalid-input/semantic controls, plus three actual source mutations of projection, averaging and missing-fibre arithmetic, each rejected under optimized Python.
- Warning-strict normal and optimized registered checks, metadata/pins, committed-byte/source-history preflight, syntax/function-bound/tabnanny diagnostics, official export integrity, and read-only Git-free normal/optimized replay.

Both registered commands were timed locally at about 1.11 seconds each; the complete registered runner took 2.45 seconds, below the individual 120-second limits. These are replay durations, not performance comparisons. No registered local check was deferred to CI. The verifier prints a generated receipt bound to all five package files.

Reproduce from the repository root, with the standard library:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -I -B research/eight-source-singleton-floor/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -I -O -B research/eight-source-singleton-floor/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/eight-source-singleton-floor
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/eight-source-singleton-floor --check-source-history
```

Another CPython 3.12 path may replace the local interpreter. Expected marker: `PASS_EIGHT_SOURCE_SINGLETON_FLOOR 28<=f(8)<=32 queries>=538 upper=542`.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The universal conclusions rest on the written proof and the cited `f(7)=24` theorem, including its published classification premises. Finite replay corroborates the new implications. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

Attainment at 28 source calls or 538 queries is unresolved. The model requires immutable binary sources, one restored dirty connector, separate unit-price singleton injections/readouts and offline outputs. Physical callers, setup, routing, stock, precision/tape, compiler admission, a complete recursive bill and a multiplication theorem remain unprovided. No selected frontier, frozen evidence or predecessor files change. Selected cold replay, Lean, Docker and a new eight-source word census were not run.

This changes the `connector-alphabet-change` card to the explicit source-count side question; TASK.json records the reason and stopping rule. The card's first positive control and selected-source metadata orientation passed separately. Final cached overlap covered 345 open PRs and 4,454 Discussion records, with incomplete sparse local metadata plus targeted all-main README and merged-PR searches. Unpublished work and arbitrary diffs remain outside that coverage.

## Open next questions

1. Does a universal 28-step word with the forced multiplicity pattern exist? Begin with a bounded exact prefix-difference search.
2. Is the complete query minimum 538, 540 or 542? Strengthen missing-mask constraints at source lengths 24 and 26 using simultaneous failed projections, or find a 28-call universal word.
3. Does a named caller expose this exact singleton interface at favourable complete prices? Bind its immutable ports and offline observations before charging setup, routing, stock, precision and restoration.

## Related open work

- #4079 studies seven-source binary weight-at-most-four demand; this uses eight sources and all nonzero binary masks. No common optimum is computed.
- #3909 adds atomic arity-four source operations to five-source binary demand; this retains singleton injections and unit complete-call prices.
- #3897 studies joint output readouts at a one-source/two-output boundary; this retains separate readouts and eight immutable sources.
- #5201 proves a signed three-source characteristic-zero connector optimum; this uses an unsigned binary eight-source alphabet and a new projection lower bound, with no shared numerical quantity.
